entries.note: Kinders 2008 (PMID 18980982) resolves; quote verbatim in abstract. Veliparib is a member; opening untested at model_first_use_year correct.

Kummar 2009 (PMID 19364967, epub 2009-04) resolves; quote verbatim. Same PAR ELISA design as the Kinders model; proximal readout; mixed advanced cancers acceptable for engagement. Pairing correctly marked comparison_stated false.
Jones 2009 (PMID 19873981) quote verbatim. model_filed true confirmed: the 2017 niraparib review cites BRCA1/2-deficient xenografts and HRD PDX models.

Quote verbatim in bundle 208447 MultidisciplineR clin-pharm (p.10-22); the review also states >=50% PBMC PARP inhibition from 80 mg. Target reached, NOVA positive -> same; margin_stated false is right (no nonclinical margin stated).
Jones 2009 quote verbatim in abstract; BRCA-selective cell killing and BRCA1-deficient xenograft activity; opening untested correct.

Mirza 2016 (PMID 27717299, epub 2016-10-07) quote verbatim; NCT01847274 results first posted 2019-05-01 and gBRCA PFS is a registered primary outcome. Should add ARIEL4 OS detriment as outcome_tested (see missing).

Quote verbatim in 209115 review; next sentence says patients' ALT/AST rises were absent in animals. same+partial is defensible under the partial clause, but a strict silence-contradicted reading gives contra; raised as rule question.
Quote verbatim; BP +13-20% at 1 mg/kg = 0.7x unbound Cmax; label grade 3-4 hypertension 9% vs 2%. Status fine, but model_change: true is misused (no preceding contra); should be false.

Berek 2018 (PMID 29767688) conclusion quoted verbatim (abstract). Decision-tree on NOVA safety population; untested at 2018 is right, prediction_level patient fits a rule choosing per-patient start dose. Not a retrodiction: NORA/PRIMA ISD outcomes unknown then.

NORA (PMID 33453391, epub Jan 2021) conclusion verbatim; 249 ISD, 235 at 200 mg, PFS HR 0.32. Prospective test, so same not retro. NORA lacks an FSD arm; Mirza 2023 PRIMA (PMID 37060236) confirms similar efficacy, better haem safety with ISD.

missing: ARIEL4 (rucaparib vs chemotherapy, BRCA-mutant relapsed ovarian; NCT02855944, results posted 2022-02-11): primary invPFS met (Kristeleit, Lancet Oncol 2022), but final OS 19.4 vs 25.4 months (Lancet Oncol 2025, PIIS1470-2045(24)00674-0); FDA treatment indication voluntarily withdrawn June 2022. Status stays same on the primary endpoint, but efficacy should carry this as a patient_trials item / outcome_tested: negative.
NOVA final OS (gBRCA HR ~0.85, not significant; non-gBRCA OS detriment) led to the 2022 restriction of niraparib 2L maintenance to gBRCA; relevant to outcome_tested, not to the PFS-based status.

Stenoparib (2X-121, member) phase 2 NCT03878849 in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer, DRP-selected not BRCA-selected; sponsor press releases only (Allarity 2025), positive in tone, outside the BRCA/HRD population; no failure to add.
rule_questions: Safety: when an FDA review says animal findings were 'consistent with' the dose-limiting harms but explicitly notes a common patient harm the species could have shown (rucaparib ALT/AST, 74% incidence) was absent, is that same + partial or contra (silence contradicted)?

Efficacy: does outcome_tested apply when the trial primary endpoint (PFS) is met but later OS shows detriment (ARIEL4) — i.e. is PFS a 'surrogate the model predicted' in oncology, and should an OS detriment ever move an efficacy cell?
model_change: is it meaningful on an entry that follows a same (not contra) entry with a different model, or should lint reject model_change: true unless the previous entry is contra?
